issue.title: Align Go proxy URL normalization in adapter builds
issue.body:
Aligns request URL handling in adapter-built Go proxies with the JavaScript adapter, so `proxy.go` sees the same paths in adapter builds as it does under `next start`.

**Validation**

- Extended `test/e2e/app-dir/native-proxy-go` for both self-hosted and adapter-built executables, including i18n, i18n domains, basePath, and `skipProxyUrlNormalize` variants. Adapter tests run the emitted executable directly and assert the URL `proxy.go` receives for each input.
- Added Rust unit tests for rendering the handler template configuration.
- Compiled the Go template locally and ran the e2e fixture's `proxy.go` against it as a standalone executable; the new adapter assertions pass with this change and fail without it.
- The full Rust crate could not be compiled locally; relying on CI.

issue.title: Preserve Request Insights history with gzip rotation
issue.body:
### What?

Preserve development Request Insights history across journal size limits and dev-server restarts, and make retained requests available through existing MCP ID filters and DevTools detail lookups.

### Why?

The journal currently truncates its contents when it reaches its size limit and at startup, discarding diagnostics that may still be needed to investigate a request.

### How?

- Store the active NDJSON journal and gzip archives in `.next/dev/request-insights/`, preserving them through both bundlers' startup cleanup. Leave the legacy journal untouched.
- Rotate at 10 MiB and on startup by renaming rather than truncating. Archives have readable UTC request-time ranges; compression preserves the source until successful publication.
- Prune by rotation age (7 days) and compressed size (100 MiB), always protecting the newest archive. Retry interrupted compression and keep maintenance failures nonfatal.
- Serialize reads and maintenance with writes. Historical ID lookups stream archives chronologically without indexes; recent queries, schemas, and CLI behavior remain unchanged. Historical scans can delay diagnostic appends on the shared queue.

### Verification

- 61 focused Request Insights/span-store tests passed, including real-file rotation, recovery, retention, and malformed-history cases.
- Restart/lock integration passed with both Turbopack and Webpack, verifying that distinct older and newly rotated requests remain accessible through HTTP/MCP.
- Package types, changed-file lint/format checks, and diff checks passed.
- Full Request Insights browser matrix and production integration suites were not run; the change is confined to dev diagnostics.

issue.title: [rollup] Read decorator options from tsconfig in the workflow transform
issue.body:
### What

Nitro and Nuxt builds of a standalone app failed on workflow files with TypeScript decorators, and this PR makes the Rollup transform turn on decorator parsing when the tsconfig asks for it.

Hi everyone, hope you're doing well! Fixes #5510. This follows the approach I floated in the issue, and it leans entirely on the tsconfig work from #757 and #5303, so thank you to everyone there.

**What this code is for**

`workflowTransformPlugin()` in `@workflow/rollup` runs SWC with the workflow plugin in step mode over every file that has `"use step"` or `"use workflow"`. `@workflow/nitro` puts it first in `rollup:before` ([nitro/src/index.ts#L104-L113](https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/e379eaf6a07696c904c28ee494cc128af2e2c772/packages/nitro/src/index.ts#L104-L113)), and `@workflow/nuxt` goes through Nitro, so it sees raw TypeScript before anything else lowers it.

### Why

**Before this PR**

A developer with `experimentalDecorators: true` in `tsconfig.json` runs `nitro build` on an app whose `workflows/order.ts` has an `@Injectable()` class next to a `'use step'` function.

1. Nitro's Rollup build calls the `transform` hook of `workflowTransformPlugin()` on `workflows/order.ts`.
2. The hook builds `jsc.parser` as only `{ syntax: 'typescript', tsx }` ([rollup/src/index.ts#L148-L174](https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/e379eaf6a07696c904c28ee494cc128af2e2c772/packages/rollup/src/index.ts#L148-L174)), with no `decorators`, and `jsc.transform` has no `legacyDecorator` or `decoratorMetadata`.
3. SWC reaches `@Injectable()` with decorator parsing off.
4. The build fails with `x Expression expected` (or ``Unexpected token `@` `` on a method decorator).

**After this PR**

Same developer, same `nitro build`.

1. Same as above through step 1.
2. The hook calls `getCachedDecoratorOptions(process.cwd())` from `@workflow/builders`. This is the function `applySwcTransform` already used internally, now exported so both places share one cache. It finds the nearest `tsconfig.json` or `jsconfig.json`, follows `extends`, and reads it once per directory.
3. `experimentalDecorators: true` gives `decorators: true` and `legacyDecorator: true`, plus `decoratorMetadata: true` when `emitDecoratorMetadata` is also on ([config-helpers.ts#L52-L62](https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/e379eaf6a07696c904c28ee494cc128af2e2c772/packages/builders/src/config-helpers.ts#L52-L62)).
4. SWC parses the decorators, lowers them to `_ts_decorate(...)`, and the step registers as `step//./workflows/order//chargeOrder`.
5. With `experimentalDecorators` off or no tsconfig at all, all three values are `false`, so the transform behaves exactly as it does today.

![On main, getDecoratorOptionsForDirectory has one caller, getDecoratorOptions in builders apply-swc-transform.ts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/abhiramshaji-cyber/Architect/pr-assets/workflow-decorators/main-decorator-options.png)

On `main`, `getDecoratorOptionsForDirectory` has one caller, `getDecoratorOptions` in `builders/src/apply-swc-transform.ts`, and nothing in `@workflow/rollup` reads the tsconfig, Functions view in [Architect](https://github.com/abhiramshaji-cyber/Architect)

**The change**

- `packages/rollup/src/index.ts`: the `transform` hook passes `decorators` into `jsc.parser` and `legacyDecorator` / `decoratorMetadata` into `jsc.transform`, matching the Next loader ([next/src/loader.ts#L266-L304](https://github.com/vercel/workflow/blob/e379eaf6a07696c904c28ee494cc128af2e2c772/packages/next/src/loader.ts#L266-L304)). That is the fix.
- `packages/builders/src/apply-swc-transform.ts` and `index.ts`: the private `getDecoratorOptions` cache becomes the exported `getCachedDecoratorOptions`, so Rollup reuses it instead of keeping a second copy (thanks VaguelySerious for the suggestion). `applySwcTransform` behaves the same.

**What changes for a user**

- Nitro and Nuxt builds of an app that has its own `tsconfig.json` at the project root now accept class and method decorators in workflow files when `experimentalDecorators` is on, including when it comes from an `extends` base.
- In a monorepo where `experimentalDecorators` lives only in the app's tsconfig, the Nitro build can still fail: `@workflow/nitro` passes `workspaceDir` as `projectRoot` to `applySwcTransform`, so the builders bundle looks up the tsconfig from the workspace root. That path predates this PR, and I am happy to open a follow up for it.
- Apps without `experimentalDecorators` see no change. Standard (non legacy) decorators stay off, the same as in Next and `applySwcTransform`.
- Vite based setups (SvelteKit, Astro, `nitro/vite`) get the same options; there Vite has usually lowered the decorators already, so nothing changes for them.
- I looked up the tsconfig from `process.cwd()`, which is what the Next loader does and what the plugin already uses for `workflowId`. Would you rather it look from the file's own folder instead, so a workspace package with its own tsconfig gets its own settings? Happy to switch if that fits better.
- Like `applySwcTransform`, the options are cached for the life of the process, so changing `experimentalDecorators` during `nitro dev` needs a restart.

### How did you test your changes?

- `packages/rollup/src/decorators.test.ts` runs the plugin against temp projects: flag on with metadata, flag on through `extends`, flag off, and only `emitDecoratorMetadata`. For each it checks the options passed to SWC and then runs the real `@swc/core` with the workflow plugin on a file with a class decorator, a method decorator and a `'use step'` function. Decorators parse when on, and the same file still fails to parse when off. The on cases fail on `main`. Each temp project is removed in `onTestFinished`.
- The no tsconfig case now lives in `packages/builders/src/config-helpers.test.ts` as `getDecoratorOptionsFromTsConfig(undefined)`, so it no longer depends on what sits above the OS temp dir.
- Ran the repro from #5510 against the built package: it now prints the `_ts_decorate` output and the registered step, and with the flag off it still throws `Expression expected`.
- `pnpm biome check`, `tsc --noEmit` for `@workflow/rollup` and `@workflow/builders`, `pnpm --filter @workflow/rollup test` (14 passed) and the builders `config-helpers` tests (12 passed). I couldn't build the Rust wasm locally, so the tests ran against the published `@workflow/swc-plugin@5.0.2` wasm.

### PR Checklist - Required to merge

- [x] 📦 `pnpm changeset` was run to create a changelog for this PR
- [x] 🔒 DCO sign-off passes (run `git commit --signoff` on your commits)
- [ ] 📝 Ping `@vercel/workflow` in a comment once the PR is ready, and the above checklist is complete

_Written by Claude Opus 5.5_

comment.body: Hey @VaguelySerious, hope you're doing well, and thanks again for the review! I resolved the three threads since the changes are in a926b6f9 and e4823d81, but two questions from them are still open. For the monorepo case, would you like a follow up that looks up the tsconfig from the app's `workingDir`/`rootDir` in builders instead of the workspace root? And would a small follow up that registers the tsconfig paths as watch files, like the Next loader does, be worth it? Also, does moving the no tsconfig case into builders work for you? Happy to adjust whichever way you prefer.

issue.title: bench: track eve build time and peak memory on a large project
issue.body:
### Summary

The nightly benchmark's only `eve build` subject is `minimal`, an agent with no tools and no sandbox, and it records time but not memory. That project can't show the regression #6571 fixed: on a project whose tools share one large module and whose agent has a sandbox, sandbox prewarm evaluated every module separately, so build memory and time grew with the tool count. This adds a `large` startup subject shaped like #6571's 80-tool benchmark and records `eve build`'s peak memory, so a return of that regression shows on eve-evals' Trends page.

On a 2 vCPU / 4 GB sandbox, the new `large` subject's `eve build` measured:

| eve | Peak memory | Build | `sandbox.prewarm` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before #6571 (8aae3e6) | 2.31 GB | 45.2 s | 35.5 s |
| main (06ee19a) | 1.03–1.08 GB | 6.7–8.0 s | 0.03–0.14 s |

### Changes

+# Pause a schedule when its turn fails
+
+> **AI status:** Written entirely by AI; human review pending.
+
+## Summary
+
+A dynamic schedule's `run` sends a message to a channel, and that message starts a session. eve
+calls `run` with a [`ScheduleHandle`][handle], so `run` can pause or delete the schedule. It does
+that before it sends anything. When a failure shows up later, inside the turn, no authored code
+holds the handle.
+
+Some failures repeat on every occurrence. Take an agent that charges each person's scheduled runs
+to that person's own AI Gateway budget. Once the budget is spent, the first model call of every
+later run fails the same way, so the agent should pause the schedule on the first failure and tell
+the person once. Today the turn fails, `run` has already returned, and the schedule keeps firing.
+
+This doc proposes `turnFailed`, a handler on `defineDynamicSchedules` next to `run`. eve calls it
+when a scheduled turn fails, and passes it the same `ScheduleHandle` as `run`. The schedule
+definition keeps its control over the schedule, and eve decides when to call it.
+
+## Authoring API
+
+```ts
+import { defineDynamicSchedules } from "eve/experimental/schedules";
+
+export default defineDynamicSchedules({
+  inputSchema: TaskInput,
+  auth: ({ principal }) => currentAccess(principal),
+  async run({ payload, occurrence, to }) {
+    await to(slack, { channelId: payload.channelId }).send(prompt(payload, occurrence));
+  },
+  async turnFailed({ error, payload, occurrence, auth, schedule }) {
+    if (error.code !== "BUDGET_SPENT") return;
+    await schedule.disable();
+    await notifyRunner(auth, payload, "Your budget is used up, so I paused this task.");
+  },
+});
+```
+
+`turnFailed` receives `ScheduleTurnFailedArgs`, exported from `eve/experimental/schedules`:
+
+| Field        | Type                         | Purpose                                                                           |
+| ------------ | ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| `error`      | `ErrorInfo`                  | The error on the failed turn's `turn.settled`, with its `code` and `message`.     |
+| `occurrence` | `ScheduleOccurrenceIdentity` | The occurrence that started the turn. Its `executionId` keys idempotent effects.  |
+| `auth`       | `SessionAuthContext`         | The occurrence's auth, as the definition's `auth` resolved it.                    |
+| `payload`    | `TPrepared`                  | The schedule's stored payload when `turnFailed` runs, including any later update. |
+| `schedule`   | `ScheduleHandle`             | `disable()` and `delete()`, as in `run` and `auth`.                               |
+| `sessionId`  | `string`                     | The session of the failed turn.                                                   |
+
+A named scope can replace `turnFailed`, as it replaces `run`.
+
+## Behavior
+
+### Which turns
+
+eve calls `turnFailed` for a turn when both hold:
+
+- The turn's context carries the schedule's provenance: the collection, the instance, and the
+  occurrence. eve sets these keys when it dispatches an occurrence ([`channel/schedule.ts`][keys]),
+  and they reach the turn as `ctx.session.schedule` ([`session-schedule.ts`][provenance]).
+- The turn settles with `outcome: "failed"`, or the session ends with `outcome: "failed"` and the
+  turn as its cause. Both come from the same failure path ([`transitions.ts`][fail]).
+
+eve doesn't call it for:
+
+- **A cancelled turn.** A person's stop and a hook's `ctx.cancel()` both settle with
+  `outcome: "cancelled"`. The author's own code chose to stop, so the schedule has nothing to learn.
+- **A completed turn.** A turn that answers with an apology still completed.
+- **A failure before any turn.** `auth` returning `null`, `run` throwing, and an exhausted retry
+  budget already reach `events["occurrence.failed"]` ([consumer route][occurrence-failed]).
+
+### How often
+
+An occurrence starts a fresh session for each send ([`channel/schedule.ts`][fresh]), so each failed
+session gets one call. A `run` that sends to two channels can get two calls for one occurrence.
+`schedule.disable()` is idempotent, and `occurrence.executionId` keys other effects, as the docs
+already advise for `run`.
+
+### Where it runs
+
+eve runs `turnFailed` in the session's workflow, after it saves the `turn.settled` line, at the
+point where hooks see the same event ([hooks guide][hooks]). A replayed step doesn't call it a
+second time.
+
+If `turnFailed` throws, eve logs the error and doesn't retry. The turn has already failed, and the
+next occurrence fires as scheduled. This matches how eve treats a hook that throws between turns.
+
+### One-time schedules
+
+A `single` schedule fires once, so `disable()` changes nothing. `delete()` still removes the
+record, and `turnFailed` can notify the person either way.
+
+## Design
+
+eve already has every piece except the call:
+
+1. **Provenance.** The turn's context holds the collection and the instance. eve adds the
+   schedule's provider namespace to the same scope, since the provider needs it to act on the
+   schedule. Today eve derives the namespace from the stored scope at dispatch
+   ([`dispatch-occurrence.ts`][namespace]), and the turn can't reach that scope.

+/**

+  private _options: Required<
+    Pick<
+      WorkerPoolOptions,

+      | 'maxWorkers'
+      | 'concurrencyPerWorker'

+  private _stdout: PassThrough

+  private _stderr: PassThrough

+  private _timeoutInterval: ReturnType<typeof setInterval> | null = null

+      enableWorkerThreads: options.enableWorkerThreads ?? false,
+      sanitizeArgs: options.sanitizeArgs ?? true,

+  // Public API

+  /**

+      errorProperties != null &&

+            errorName

+        : Error

+  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+  // Internal: exit and error handling

+  /**

+    // in-flight requests that the child didn't respond to before exiting.
+    if (worker.state === WorkerState.SHUTTING_DOWN) {
+      this._rejectActiveRequests(
+        worker,
+        new Error('Worker exited during shutdown')
+      )
+      return
+    }
+
+    // Notify the caller about the unexpected exit
+    this._options.onWorkerExit?.(code, signal)
+
+    // Reject all in-flight requests and remove from pool
+    this._rejectActiveRequests(worker, new WorkerExitError(code, signal))
+
+    this._allWorkers.delete(worker)
+    this._availableWorkers.delete(worker)
+
+    // Offer queued tasks to any already-available workers before spawning new
+    // ones; this avoids unnecessary cold-boot latency when idle workers exist.
+    if (!this._ending) {
+      for (const available of this._availableWorkers) {
+        if (this._taskQueue.length === 0) break
+        this._drainQueue(available)
+      }
+      this._spawnForQueuedTasks()
+    }
+  }
+
+  /**
+   * Handle a worker whose module failed to load (require() threw). Unlike a
+   * setup() failure the worker can't serve any CALL, and every worker loads
+   * the same module, so reject its in-flight requests and all queued tasks
+   * with the load error, then remove and kill the worker. Its exit is
+   * expected: it isn't reported via onWorkerExit or respawned. A later
+   * dispatch() spawns a fresh worker.
+   */
+  private _handleLoadError(
+    worker: PoolWorker,
+    message: Extract<ParentMessage, [typeof PARENT_MESSAGE_LOAD_ERROR, ...any]>
+  ): void {
+    const [, errorName, errorMessage, errorStack] = message
+    const error: Error & { type?: unknown } = new Error(
+      'Error when loading worker module: ' + errorMessage
+    )
+    error.type = errorName
+    error.stack = errorStack
+
+    if (worker.state === WorkerState.BOOTING) {
+      this._bootingCount--
+    }
+    // SHUTTING_DOWN makes _handleExit treat the upcoming exit as expected
+    worker.state = WorkerState.SHUTTING_DOWN
+    this._allWorkers.delete(worker)
+    this._availableWorkers.delete(worker)
+
+    this._rejectActiveRequests(worker, error)
+    for (const task of this._taskQueue) {
+      task.reject(error)
+    }
+    this._taskQueue = []
+
+    worker.handle.forceKill()
+  }
+
+  /**
+   * Handle errors on the child process itself (e.g. ENOMEM, EMFILE, failed
+   * to spawn). These are distinct from errors thrown by worker code.
+   * Rejects in-flight requests and also rejects any queued tasks since the
+   * spawn failure likely indicates a system-level problem (ENOMEM, EMFILE).
+   */
+  private _handleSpawnError(worker: PoolWorker, error: Error): void {
+    this._rejectActiveRequests(worker, error)
+
+    // Remove the failed worker from the pool and fix the booting count so
+    // _canSpawnWorker() doesn't permanently see a phantom worker.
+    if (worker.state === WorkerState.BOOTING) {
+      this._bootingCount--
+    }
+    this._allWorkers.delete(worker)
+    this._availableWorkers.delete(worker)
+
+    // Also reject all queued tasks — spawn errors typically indicate a
+    // system-level problem that would affect new workers too.
+    for (const task of this._taskQueue) {
+      task.reject(error)
+    }

Done in 1deccd01dfbca4b2c42253395d4b9347d58347f6. Same for spawn errors: queued tasks are rejected only when no worker is left. The errored worker is also marked `SHUTTING_DOWN` and force-killed, so a following `exit` is not reported or double-counted. Tests cover both cases.

issue.title: Let a dynamic system instruction share the prompt cache across sessions
issue.body:
Since #6151, eve sends dynamic system instructions after the system cache breakpoint, which assumes they differ per session. A tenant-scoped `defineDynamic` instruction, as the instructions guide suggests, is the same for every session of that tenant. Each new session therefore writes it to the cache again. Our agent serves several locations, each with a ~1.3k-token location block, using a direct Anthropic model with a 1h TTL. All four breakpoints are already in use, so we can't add one.

Second new session at the same location, eve 1.0.2, Sonnet 5.5:

|  | Cache read | Cache write |
| --- | --- | --- |
| eve 1.0.2 | 6,562 | 1,406 |
| Breakpoint moved after the location block | 7,871 | 96 |

**Ask:** an opt-in that puts the system breakpoint after a shared dynamic instruction, keeping the last-tool breakpoint as the default (#5811 relies on it):

```ts
return defineInstructions({ content, cache: "shared" });
```

**Workaround:** a `wrapLanguageModel` middleware that moves the last tool's marker onto the second system message, as in #4050. It depends on eve's internal layout and isn't visible in traces (#4203).

Related: #6151, #5811, #4050, #4203

comment.body: Replace: move the system breakpoint from after the base to after the last shared instruction. The count stays at four, the last-tool one stays put, and sessions without a shared instruction are unchanged. The base is still read from cache, since it's a prefix of each shared entry; different tenants each write their own copy of the shared block once.

Correction: the workflow already covers this. It regenerates every type in `MODALITY_CONFIG` and diffs `gateway-*-model-settings.ts`, so your `extraction` entry plus the seed file is enough. issue.title: fix(eve): renew Vercel sandbox timeouts during active operations
issue.body:
### Summary

Vercel sandboxes currently stop at a fixed deadline even when eve is running a command, interrupting training, builds, and other active work. This change renews the timeout inside the Vercel provider while sandbox operations remain active. It replaces the broader approach in #6582 without introducing a background-job API or changing session scheduling. Related to #6553.

### Changes

- Extend Vercel session timeouts before operations when needed and periodically during commands, file transfers, and sandbox initialization.
- Stop renewal when work completes, is canceled, or its execution scope ends, without removing compute from existing shutdown tracking.
- Serialize extension requests and retry transient failures without failing the underlying operation; renewal never resumes stopped compute.
- Preserve sandbox-handle reuse after an explicit stop within the same execution scope, including when reuse overlaps stop cleanup.
- Let queued terminal cleanup proceed if an earlier native stop fails, while preserving the error for the original stop caller.
- Keep the 30-minute default and Vercel's maximum session duration; no public API, Docker, idle-stop, or background-job lifetime changes.

issue.title: fix(middleware): forward empty _rsc parameter on rewrite for RSC requests (#100398)
issue.body:
Closes #100398

### What?
Ensures that an empty `_rsc` search parameter (e.g. `/target?_rsc`) is forwarded to the rewritten destination URL for RSC requests.

### Why?
In `packages/next/src/server/web/adapter.ts`, the check:
```typescript
if (response && rewrite && isRSCRequest && rscHash) {
```
evaluates to `false` when `rscHash` is an empty string (`""`).

During Server Action `redirect()`, `createRedirectRenderResult` deletes `Next-Router-State-Tree` and fetches `/target?_rsc` with an empty hash, which is valid and expected per `base-server.ts` ("When no headers are present, expectedHash is empty string and client must send `_rsc` param").

When `rscHash` is dropped by middleware on external rewrites or proxy destinations that only see the rewritten URL:
1. The destination server sees no `_rsc` query param (`actualHash` is `null`).
2. `expectedHash === actualHash` (`"" === null`) fails.
3. The server responds with `307 -> /target?_rsc`.
4. The client/undici fetch follows the redirect back through the same rewrite, the hash is dropped again, causing an infinite redirect loop until undici aborts with `TypeError: fetch failed (redirect count exceeded)`.

### How?
Updated the condition to check `rscHash !== null`:
```typescript
if (response && rewrite && isRSCRequest && rscHash !== null) {
```
This ensures:
- When `_rsc` is present (even if empty `""`), it is preserved and set on the rewritten URL.
- When `_rsc` was not present in the incoming request (`null`), no parameter is added.
- Added comprehensive unit tests in `test/unit/web-runtime/adapter-rsc-rewrite.test.ts` covering empty `_rsc`, non-empty `_rsc`, non-RSC requests, and RSC requests with no `_rsc`.
